excerpt: BPI Ps 3 sitao is a pole sitao variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1982. Its record notes 12.77 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 12.77 t/ha beats the average of its group, 11.33. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It was weak against rust, so scout for it from the early weeks.

The pests and diseases that hit sitao fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant BPI Ps 3 sitao

It is recommended for the dry season. Pole sitao climbs a trellis and bears for weeks, while bush sitao needs no trellis and comes in at once. Pick long, dark green pods that snap cleanly, and a variety rated against the bean fly and rust if you can. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).
